messages:
eli_support: FYI customer 'AcmeMaps' opened a high-priority ticket — p99 latency spike after we onboarded Lumina-v2. p50 unchanged, p95 ~2x, p99 ~4x for long-context (>16k tokens). Request IDs: r-8a3f2, r-8a3f8. Link to sample: https://s3.redwood/acmemaps/lumina-v2-sample.txt

mike_oncall: any infra deploys or tokenizer changes in the last 24h? :eyes:

deploy-bot: [deploy] lumina-v2/tokenizer-merge v1.3.0 deployed by ci-bot at 2026-03-15T10:12:09Z (sha: a1b2c3)

anya_eng-runtime: I'll take triage. Can customer share a minimal repro (curl + payload) and whether they used chunking/streaming?

carla_customer: attaching sample and minimal curl. We're not chunking, sending full context. Repro payload (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_acme_***' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"lumina-v2","input":"<20k chars>...","max_tokens":1024}'
```
Observed latency: 5.2s p99, previously ~1.1s on lumina-v1.

eli_support: ran local repro with their payload; profile shows tokenize stage ~1.6s (dominant), model forward ~2.8s. On lumina-v1 tokenize was ~0.15s for same input.

anya_eng-runtime: interesting — tokenizer step jumped a lot. Initial hypothesis: the new BPE merge changes (v3) added extra normalization pass for CJK and long-run merges. Can you paste a small profiler snippet?

eli_support: profiler snippet (top timings):
```
0. tokenization_bpe_merge_v3: 1600ms
1. kv_cache_lookup: 120ms
2. model_forward: 2800ms
3. postprocess: 40ms
```

mike_oncall: @anya any quick mitigation we can do without rolling back entire deploy? Maybe force legacy tokenizer for long inputs or route large sequences to lumina-v1?

anya_eng-runtime: quick mitigations we can try (in order):
- route requests with estimated seq_len > 16000 to lumina-v1 fallback.
- set header X-Tokenizer: legacy to force old codepath (supported temporarily).
- increase kv cache window to reduce repeated tokenization for streaming chunk workloads (lower impact here).
I'll open a rollout patch to add header-based override and a routing rule.

eli_support: added a temporary routing rule in staging; sample test shows p99 drop to ~1.2s for the same payload when forcing legacy tokenizer.

deploy-bot: [change] routing rule added: support/longseq-fallback -> lumina-v1 by eli_support at 2026-03-15T11:02:14Z

anya_eng-runtime: created ENG-4521: "Lumina-v2 tokenizer regressions on long-context" and PR: https://git.redwood/infra/patches/789 (adds header override + routing condition). Assigning to eng-runtime for deeper root cause.

carla_customer: applied header override on our side (X-Tokenizer: legacy) and p99 dropped to 1.0s in our staging load. Thanks — we'll keep production traffic on the fallback rule for now and monitor.

mike_oncall: logging action items: 1) short-term: keep routing rule for sequences >16000 2) eng-runtime to investigate bpe_merge_v3 perf on long runs (ENG-4521) 3) add automated canary to detect tokenizer cost regressions on large inputs 4) consider revert or optimized implementation.

anya_eng-runtime: working on micro-benchmarks now. Early suspicion: worst-case quadratic behavior in merge pass for long runs with pathological merge tables. I'll post perf diffs and a targeted patch today.

deploy-bot: [metric] post-fallback p99 for lumina-v2 long-context sample decreased from 5.2s -> 1.1s (10:30Z checks).

eli_support: communicated workaround to customer and updated support playbook (added header + routing workaround). Closing escalation if metrics hold; keeping ENG-4521 open for root-cause and permanent fix. :white_check_mark:
